svg.title: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to fix — Every check stops and names the fix, then finishes cleanly once nothing is missing
svg.text: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to
Scenario: Every check stops and names the fix, then finishes cleanly once nothing is missing
The check names each missing tool
The check reads the right GitLab host
init names the exact fix, then bows out cleanly

g.text: Given a fresh toolbox checkout with none of its UI tools installed yet
A throwaway toolbox checkout before any setup: gum, glow and the glab CLI are all missing.
The card lists the three, none installed.
When the developer runs the auth check straight away
With nothing installed the check stops at the first tool, gum: "Required UI dependency
missing: gum", pointing at task dev:setup-environment.
When the developer installs gum and re-runs the check
With gum in place the check moves on and stops at the next tool, glow: "Required UI
dependency missing: glow".
When the developer adds glow and re-runs, leaving only the CLI missing
With gum and glow in place the check clears the UI tools and stops at the CLI: the "GitLab
CLI not found" box tells you to install glab.
When the developer installs the CLI and re-runs it in CI mode, still
not signed in
Every tool is installed but no GitLab sign-in yet; CI=true takes the non-interactive path:
"GitLab authentication required", pointing at task glab:auth.
Given a self-hosted GitLab project with the tools installed but no
sign-in yet
A throwaway project whose remote points at a self-hosted GitLab host — a company running its
own GitLab — with gum, glow and glab installed but no sign-in yet. The card shows the
remote.
Then the check reads the self-hosted GitLab host straight from the
remote
CI mode takes the non-interactive path: "GitLab authentication required", naming the exact
self-hosted host it read from the remote.
When the same project instead uses an SSH-style gitlabssh remote
The origin is switched to an SSH-style gitlabssh.* URL — the address a self-hosted GitLab
gives out for SSH clones. The card shows the new remote.
Then the check turns it back into the gitlab API host
The gitlabssh.* remote is turned back into its gitlab.* API host: the message names
gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example and never the ssh name.
Given a developer's new project points at a GitLab remote the CLI never
signed into
A throwaway project whose only link to GitLab is a remote the CLI never signed into. Set up
off-camera: a fresh Ubuntu box with the toolbox and this git remote.
Then init stops and prints the exact GitLab sign-in command to run
init installs its tools, reaches the sign-in check and stops with "GitLab authentication
required", pointing at task glab:auth.
When another developer's project points at a GitHub remote instead
A new project whose remote points at github.com — a non-GitLab host init must never push to.
The card shows the remote.
Then init refuses the non-GitLab remote and shows how to fix it
init finds no GitLab remote and stops with "No GitLab repository remote was detected.",
giving the exact git remote set-url line to fix it.
Then init finishes cleanly once the GitLab integration is turned off
TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false makes every glab step skip, so init reaches "DevSecOps project
initialization completed" and never asks about sign-in.
